endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: Additional research is required to understand clinician experience with ambient scribe, particularly in identifying which visit types are most suited to its use.

endorsements.title: Governing the attention dividend: AI-reclaimed clinician capacity as a health policy resource
endorsements.quote: Net documentation minutes saved per scheduled hour, minus verification time spent on AI-generated outputs, reported separately from changes in cognitive task load

endorsements.title: Embracing Large Language Models for Medical Applications, Part II: Building a Framework for Clinical Stewardship.
endorsements.quote: They should also be evaluated for note accuracy, concision, clinician time, patient trust, billing effects, and differential performance across specialties, languages, accents, and visit types.

evidence.title: The Influence of Artificial Intelligence Scribes on Clinician Experience and Efficiency among Pediatric Subspecialists: A Rapid, Randomized Quality Improvement Trial
evidence.outcome: Burnout, documentation time, and wRVUs (coding intensity proxy) after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Burnout dropped from 8 (89%) to 5 (56%) in intervention; no significant change in time in notes per encounter (+0.2 min) or wRVUs per encounter (-0.03, 95% CI -0.5 to +0.44).
evidence.quote: There was no significant change to pajama time (-9.4 minutes per scheduled day, 95% CI: -41.2 to +22.4), time in notes per encounter (+0.2 minutes per note, 95% CI: -6.6 to +6.9), or work Relative Value Units (wRVUs) per encounter (-0.03, 95% CI: -0.5 to +0.44).

evidence.title: Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial
evidence.outcome: Documentation time and clinician burnout after AI scribe deployment using validated instruments
evidence.effect: Improvements in Mini-Z (DAX +2.83; Nabla +2.69), PTL (DAX -39.9), and PFI-WE (DAX -0.32; Nabla -0.23) versus control; Nabla reduced time-in-note 9.5%.
evidence.quote: Increases in total Mini-Z (scale 10-50; DAX 2.83 [95% CI, +1.28 to +4.37]; Nabla +2.69 [95% CI, +1.14 to +4.23]) and reductions in PTL (scale 0-400; DAX -39.9 [95% CI, -71.9 to -7.9]; Nabla -31.7 [95% CI, -63.8 to +0.4]), and PFI-WE (scale 0-4; DAX 0.32 [95% CI,-0.55 to -0.08]; Nabla -0.23 [95% CI, -0.46 to +0.01]) scores suggest improvement for users of either scribe versus the control.

evidence.title: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being
evidence.outcome: Coding accuracy/intensity, documentation time, and burnout measured after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Burnout measure (Stanford PFI) work exhaustion fell 0.44 points; note time fell 0.36 h/day; diagnostic billing codes improved (P<0.001); professional fulfillment +0.14 (P=0.04) nonsignificant.
evidence.quote: Diagnostic billing codes improved with ambient AI use (P<0.001).

evidence.title: A Novel Playbook for Pragmatic Trial Operations to Monitor and Evaluate Ambient Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice
evidence.outcome: ICD-10 documentation accuracy monitored after ambient AI deployment
evidence.effect: Coding audits detected accuracy drop from 79% (95% CI 72-86%) to 35% (95% CI 28-42%) after template change; accuracy returned to baseline after remediation
evidence.quote: A brief workflow issue related to a note template change initially reduced ICD-10 documentation accuracy from 79% (95% confidence interval [CI], 72 to 86%) to 35% (95% CI, 28 to 42%); accuracy returned to baseline after note template redesign and user training.

evidence.title: Hybrid Ambient Clinical Documentation and Physician Performance: Work Outside of Work, Documentation Delay, and Financial Productivity
evidence.outcome: Documentation time, after-hours work, and financial productivity after ambient scribe deployment
evidence.effect: WOW decreased 41.7% (95% CI -51.8%, -29.4%) by day 50; wRVUs increased 12.1% (95% CI 5.7%, 18.9%) by day 50.
evidence.quote: Financial productivity increased steadily by 1.5% (95% CI -0.2%, 3.2%) on day 10 and 12.1% (95% CI 5.7%, 18.9%) by day 50.
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (attending physicians and advanced practice clinicians)

evidence.title: Navigating Collective Bargaining Barriers to the Implementation of AI Scribe Technology Among Ambulatory Advanced Practice Providers: Mixed Methods Quality Improvement Study
evidence.outcome: documentation time
evidence.effect: The pilot group spent a mean of 6 minutes in the note writer versus 14 minutes for the nonpilot group.
evidence.quote: The time spent in the note writer for the pilot group was a mean 6 (SD 2.2; median 6, IQR 5.0-8.0) minutes vs a mean 14 (SD 11.2; median 11, IQR 8.4-18.5) minutes for nonpilot APPs.

evidence.title: Impact of an AI medical scribe after 375 000 notes generated across care levels in a European health system
evidence.outcome: Documentation time per note and clinician stress after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Estimated documentation time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (-29%, p = 1.70e-11); ability to work without administrative stress rose from 2.41 to 3.14 (p = 2.46e-8).
evidence.quote: With the introduction of the AI medical scribe, the estimated time spent on documentation per note decreased from 6.69 minutes to 4.72 minutes (-29%, p = 1.70e-11).

evidence.title: The Effect of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Notes on Provider Burnout
evidence.outcome: Clinician burnout measured with validated instrument after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Burnout rates decreased from 69 to 43% and median burnout score fell from 4.16 to 3.16 (p = 0.005) on the Stanford PFI.
evidence.quote: Burnout rates decreased from 69 to 43%.
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers completing pre and post surveys)

evidence.title: From Burden to Balance: Trends in Documentation Workload with Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Adoption
evidence.outcome: Clinician documentation time, workload, and burnout after ambient AI scribe deployment using validated instruments
evidence.effect: Reduced mental demand, time pressure, documentation effort (p<0.05); more clinicians reporting <2 hours/day outside-clinic documentation; burnout increased across follow-up (p<0.05).
evidence.quote: Clinicians reported statistically significant reductions in mental demand, time pressure, and documentation effort at postimplementation intervals (p < 0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: clinician survey respondents at baseline (172, 117, 101 at 1-, 3-, 6-month follow-up)

evidence.title: Large-Scale Implementation of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation and Its Effects on Electronic Health Record Efficiency and Clinician Well-Being
evidence.outcome: Documentation time and clinician burnout measured after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Active note time decreased 26.2%; survey at 45 days showed most respondents reported reduced burnout; note length rose 28.8%. Coding accuracy and intensity were not measured.
evidence.quote: Survey responses (n = 233; 26.4% response rate) indicated improvements across domains, with most respondents reporting reduced burnout, increased job satisfaction, improved work-life balance, and a strong preference to continue using DAX.

evidence.title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout
evidence.outcome: Documentation time and burnout measures after ambient scribe use
evidence.effect: Time-in-note fell only with Nabla. Any scribe reduced task load (-35.8) and work exhaustion (-0.27) and raised Mini-Z (+2.76).
evidence.quote: Reductions in TL (scale 0-400, TL=-35.8 [-63.7,-7.9]; p=.01) and work exhaustion (scale 0-4, PFI-WE=-0.27 [-0.48,-0.07]; p=.01) were seen with users of any scribe.

evidence.title: Impact of AI Scribes on Physician Productivity and Workflow in Medical Oncology
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic codes per visit after AI scribe deployment (coding intensity)
evidence.effect: No change in number of diagnostic codes per visit; mean visits rose (β = 3.35, P = .010) and billing per working day rose (β = $433.61, P = .007).
evidence.quote: There was no change in the number of diagnostic codes per visit.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Impact of Artificial Intelligence Scribes on Clinical Workflow and Documentation Quality: A Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Physician and administrative documentation processing time with AI scribe versus conventional methods
evidence.effect: Statistically significant reduction in both physician and administrative processing times (P < 0.0001).
evidence.quote: Use of AI scribes resulted in a statistically significant reduction in both physician and administrative processing times (P < 0.0001).

evidence.title: The impact of nuance DAX ambient listening AI documentation: a cohort study
evidence.outcome: After-hours EHR time, productivity, documentation completion and CPT deficiency after ambient scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Statistically significant worsening of after-hours EHR time; no practical change in productivity; no significant benefits to documentation or productivity measures; positive trends in provider engagement.
evidence.quote: There was a statistically significant worsening of after-hours EHR.

evidence.title: Use of an AI Scribe and Electronic Health Record Efficiency
evidence.outcome: Clinician EHR time, note time, after-hours documentation time, and encounter closure time after AI scribe use
evidence.effect: Users had 8.5% lower mean EHR time and 15.9% lower note time versus weighted nonusers; pre-post time to close encounters fell 7.1 hours. No significant difference in after-hours documentation time or appointment volume.
evidence.quote: In this retrospective cohort study, clinicians using an AI scribe spent significantly less time in the EHR and in notes in both pre-post and propensity score analyses.
evidence.sample_unit: ambulatory clinicians (125 AI scribe users, 478 weighted nonusers)

evidence.title: Psychiatric Documentation and Management in Primary Care With Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use
evidence.outcome: Change in documentation and management of psychiatric symptoms after AI scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, or antidepressant) less likely in AI-scribed vs contemporaneous unscribed visits (aOR 0.83; 95% CI 0.72-0.95); not different for human scribes (aOR 0.97).
evidence.quote: In a multiple logistic regression model, likelihood of a psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, or antidepressant prescription) was significantly lower among AI-scribed visits compared with contemporaneous unscribed visits (adjusted odds ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.95), but not for human-scribed visits compared with contemporaneous unscribed visits (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.85-1.11).

evidence.title: Navigating Collective Bargaining Barriers to the Implementation of AI Scribe Technology Among Ambulatory Advanced Practice Providers: Mixed Methods Quality Improvement Study
evidence.outcome: Time spent in the note writer
evidence.effect: Mean note-writer time was 6 (SD 2.2) minutes for pilot APPs versus 14 (SD 11.2) minutes for nonpilot APPs.
evidence.quote: The time spent in the note writer for the pilot group was a mean 6 (SD 2.2; median 6, IQR 5.0-8.0) minutes vs a mean 14 (SD 11.2; median 11, IQR 8.4-18.5) minutes for nonpilot APPs.

evidence.title: Impact of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Notes on Provider Burnout
evidence.outcome: Clinician burnout and professional fulfillment measured with the Stanford PFI before and after ambient AI scribe use
evidence.effect: Median burnout score fell from 4.16 to 3.16 (p=0.005); burnout rate fell from 69% to 43%; work exhaustion unchanged; fulfillment 6.1 vs 6.5 (p=0.10, non-significant).
evidence.quote: Results showed a significant reduction in burnout scores, with the median burnout score improving from 4.16 to 3.16 (p=0.005), with validated Stanford PFI cutoff for overall burnout 3.33.
evidence.sample_unit: clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers) completing pre and post surveys

evidence.title: Enhancing Clinical Documentation Workflow with Ambient Artificial Intelligence: Clinician Perspectives on Work Burden, Burnout, and Job Satisfaction
evidence.outcome: Clinician-perceived documentation burden, after-hours documentation, burnout risk, and job satisfaction after ambient AI scribe
evidence.effect: Majority agreed the tool decreased documentation burden and after-hours documentation, reduced burnout risk, and increased job satisfaction; 48% agreed an additional patient could be seen.
evidence.quote: The majority of respondents agreed that the AI tool decreased documentation burden, decreased the time spent documenting outside clinical hours, reduced burnout risk, and increased job satisfaction, with 48% agreeing that an additional patient could be seen if needed.

evidence.title: The association between use of ambient voice technology documentation during primary care patient encounters, documentation burden, and provider burnout
evidence.outcome: Documentation time per encounter and provider burnout (OLBI) after ambient scribe deployment
evidence.effect: Documentation time fell 28.8% (1.8 min; 95% CI 1.4-2.2). High DAX use had lower OLBI sub-score (MD -2.1; CI -3.8 to -0.4) but not total burnout (MD -3.0; CI -6.4 to 0.3).
evidence.quote: After DAX™ implementation average documentation time in notes per encounter was significantly reduced by 28.8% (1.8 min; 95% CI 1.4-2.2).
evidence.sample_unit: primary care providers completing burnout survey (19 with pre/post documentation time data)

evidence.title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribes: physician burnout and perspectives on usability and documentation burden
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Physician task load, burnout, and usability before vs after ambient AI scribe pilot
evidence.effect: Task load fell by 24.42 points (p <.001), burnout fell by 1.94 points (p <.001), and usability rose by 10.9 points (p <.001) in paired analysis (n = 38).
evidence.quote: Paired survey analysis (n = 38) revealed large statistically significant reductions in task load (-24.42, p <.001) and burnout (-1.94, p <.001), and moderate statistically significant improvements in usability scores (+10.9, p <.001).

evidence.title: The Effect of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes on Trainee Documentation Burden
evidence.outcome: Documentation burden (NASA-TLX, TrendBurden) and time on notes after ambient scribe pilot
evidence.effect: NASA-TLX improved from 56.3 to 43.3 (p<0.001) and TrendBurden items improved. Time on notes per note showed no significant change (median +0.4 minutes, p=0.568).
evidence.quote: No significant difference in time spent on notes activity per note written was observed, with a median increase of 0.4 minutes (p = 0.568).

evidence.title: Use of Ambient AI Scribes to Reduce Administrative Burden and Professional Burnout
evidence.outcome: Clinician burnout and after-hours documentation time before and after 30 days of ambient AI scribe use
evidence.effect: Burnout fell from 51.9% to 38.8% (OR 0.26; 95% CI 0.13-0.54). After-hours documentation time improved by a mean (SE) of 0.90 (0.19) hours.
evidence.quote: After 30 days with the ambient AI scribe, the proportion of participants experiencing burnout decreased significantly from 51.9% to 38.8% (odds ratio, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.54).

evidence.title: Ambient AI-assited clinical documentation in surgical outpatient care: a preliminary study of usability, workflow, and patient experience
evidence.outcome: Billing metrics, pajama time, mental demand, and burnout after ambient AI scribe pilot
evidence.effect: Billing showed no significant changes, so no upcoding signal. Pajama time did not change (p=0.55). NASA-TLX mental demand fell 14 to 5 (p=0.08), and burnout fell from 67% to 33%.
evidence.quote: The billing metric showed no significant changes.
evidence.sample_unit: ambulatory providers (three surgeons in the surgical subgroup)

evidence.title: Implementation of Dragon Ambient Experience by Plastic Surgery Residents Improves Wellness and Decreases Burnout: A Pilot Study
evidence.venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
evidence.outcome: Clinician workload, burnout, and documentation time after ambient scribe deployment, using validated instruments
evidence.effect: NASA-TLX fell from 74.64 to 51.94 (P=0.04); after-hours documentation fell from 3.6 to 0.75 h/week (P=0.02); Mini-Z rose from 2.5 to 2.83 (P=0.73, not significant).
evidence.quote: After DAX implementation, the NASA-TLX score decreased significantly to 51.94 (P = 0.04), and documentation time dropped to 0.75 hours per week (P = 0.02).

evidence.title: The impact of artificial intelligence scribes on physician and advanced practice provider cognitive load and well-being
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Clinician burnout and intent to leave after AI scribe deployment, by professional role
evidence.effect: Physicians reported reduced burnout and intent to leave; APPs had no significant reduction in burnout or intent to leave. Both groups showed reduced cognitive task load.
evidence.quote: Physicians reported reduced burnout and intent to leave; however, APPs did not have a significant reduction in burnout or intent to leave.
evidence.sample_unit: physicians and advanced practice providers (survey respondents)

evidence.title: Ambient AI Scribe Implementation in an Ambulatory Setting in a Single Medical Group: Prospective Study
evidence.outcome: Documentation time, after-hours EMR time, and provider burnout after ambient scribe deployment
evidence.effect: High users: 21% decrease in daily note time (-13.6 min), 13% decrease in pajama time (-3.6 min). Providers with no burnout symptoms rose 22% (49.4%), but the burnout difference was not significant.
evidence.quote: This ambient AI scribe decreased the time providers spent writing notes in the clinic and decreased time spent in the EMR outside of work hours.

evidence.title: Selecting, Scaling, and Measuring the Value of Ambient AI in a Nonacademic Health System: Multiphase Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Coding level shifts and visit volume after ambient scribe pilot
evidence.effect: 3.8% increase in level 4 established patient visits (P=.05); established patient volumes up 8.5%; projected revenue gain of US $2629 per provider per month.
evidence.quote: Coding patterns shifted toward higher-complexity visits, with a 3.8% increase in level 4 established patient visits (P=.05), and established patient volumes increased by 8.5%, which was associated with a projected revenue gain of US $2629 per provider per month.

evidence.title: An Evaluation of AI-Generated Clinical Notes in the OpenNotes Era: A Thematic Analysis of Clinician Discourse
evidence.venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
evidence.outcome: Clinician concerns about upcoding and over-documentation from AI scribes
evidence.effect: Clinicians described AI-driven over-documentation and productivity demands as threatening the fiscal credibility of the record through inadvertent upcoding (qualitative theme).
evidence.quote: Finally, institutional productivity demands and AI-driven over-documentation severely threaten the fiscal credibility of the medical record through inadvertent upcoding.
evidence.sample_unit: Reddit comments (120 threads, eight clinician subreddits)

evidence.title: Evaluation of an AI Medical Scribe After 236,153 Notes Generated Across Care Levels in a European Health System: Mixed Methods Retrospective Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Self-reported documentation time per note and administrative stress before vs after AI scribe
evidence.effect: Documentation time 4.72 vs 6.69 min per note (-29%, P<.001); stress-free administrative work rating 3.14 vs 2.41 (P<.001); presence with patients 4.33 vs 3.73 (P<.001).
evidence.quote: Following the introduction of the AI medical scribe, the estimated time spent on documentation per note was lower than before (4.72 vs 6.69 minutes; -29%, P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: fully onboarded clinicians (paired survey); editing metadata from 236,153 notes by 1295 clinicians

evidence.title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribe implementation in inpatient setting
evidence.outcome: Inpatient time in notes per day before vs after ambient AI scribe implementation
evidence.effect: Mean time in notes per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (SD 25.59) to 41.6 (SD 27.3) min (p = .77); overall ambient AI utilization was 3%.
evidence.quote: Mean time in notes (SD) per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (25.59) to 41.6 (27.3) min (p = .77).

commentary.bottom_line: Ten deployment studies, three of them randomized, measured documentation time, burnout, or coding after AI scribe rollout, and their results varied by site, specialty, and tool, which suggests that local measurement may be needed to know whether a given deployment reduces burden or shifts coding. Only one quasi-experimental study shows that monitoring itself caught a problem, when coding audits detected ICD-10 accuracy falling from 79% to 35% after a template change and recovering after remediation.

perspectives.view: No study compares systems that measure these outcomes with systems that do not, so the three randomized trials test the scribe rather than the monitoring practice. Burnout or work exhaustion fell in all three, but time in notes did not change in one, and burnout rose across follow-up in a large survey. This inconsistency lowers certainty about expected effects.

Coding audits in one quasi-experimental study detected an accuracy drop from 79% to 35% after a template change, and accuracy returned to baseline after remediation. This is the only supplied example of measurement catching an error that would otherwise have persisted. A separate study found psychiatric intervention less likely in AI-scribed visits (aOR 0.83), a change that coding and time metrics may not detect.

Studies measured time in different ways, including EHR log time in notes, work outside of work, and self-reported minutes per note, which limits comparison across sites. One site found note time fell 26.2% while note length rose 28.8% and did not measure coding. Inpatient note time did not change where ambient AI utilization was 3%, suggesting that usage should be tracked alongside outcomes.

Coding intensity results differed across sites. wRVUs rose 12.1% by day 50 in one study, level 4 established visits rose 3.8% in another, and a trial found billing per day rose with more visits but no change in diagnostic codes per visit. Other sites found no billing change. Measuring coding intensity separately from visit volume may help distinguish these patterns.

One pre-post study without a comparator was conducted in Sweden in a non-English setting and reported per-note documentation time falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes. No test measured outcomes in Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy settings, where visit complexity and interpreter use may change both documentation time and coding patterns.

The recommended measures track clinicians and billing, and none of the tests reported patient-level outcomes. One hazard study found fewer psychiatric referrals, new diagnoses, or antidepressant starts in AI-scribed visits. This suggests that monitoring limited to time, burnout, and coding may miss changes in the care patients receive.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares deployments with and without structured monitoring, so the benefit of measurement itself remains untested beyond a single audit that detected and corrected a coding accuracy drop. Studies are needed that report coding accuracy against audit standards separately from coding intensity and visit volume, that report net documentation minutes after subtracting verification time, and that use common validated burnout instruments over follow-up longer than six months.
commentary.underserved_note: Only one test, conducted in a Swedish non-English setting, fell into an underserved category, and no test included Medicaid, safety-net, US limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these populations have no direct evidence on how scribe deployment affects coding, documentation time, or burnout in their settings and would depend on their own measurement.
